current.jp: 今ではめったに行われません。
current.kana: いまでわめったにおこなわれません。

structure_explanation.en: Sentence in polite, passive style. 今では (nowadays) opens it: 今 (now) + で (locative/temporal) + は (topic). Then comes the adverb めったに and the verb 行う (to carry out) in the polite passive-negative form 行われません (行わ + れ passive + ません polite negative). The めったに...ない pattern appears here in the polite ません variant, and translates as 'rarely'.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: Frase em estilo polido e passivo. 今では (hoje em dia) abre a frase: 今 (agora) + で (locativo/temporal) + は (tópico). Vem o advérbio めったに e o verbo 行う (realizar) na forma passiva-negativa polida 行われません (行わ + れ passivo + ません negativo polido). O padrão めったに...ない aparece aqui na variante polida ません, e traduz como 'raramente'.

translation_literal.en: As for now, [it] is rarely carried out (rarely, is-not-carried-out).
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a agora, raramente não é realizado.

translation.pt-BR: Hoje em dia raramente se faz isso.

note.en: めった + に form the adverb めったに
note.pt-BR: めった + に forma o advérbio めったに

note.en: に that turns めった into めったに
note.pt-BR: に que transforma めった em めったに

note.en: stem of 行う (行わ-) prepared for the passive
note.pt-BR: raiz de 行う (行わ-) preparada para a passiva

note.en: れる in the form れ, forming the passive 行われる
note.pt-BR: れる na forma れ, formando a passiva 行われる

note.en: ます in the form ませ, required by the polite negation
note.pt-BR: ます na forma ませ, exigida pela negação polida

note.en: ん (from ぬ), negation that with ませ forms ません, completing めったに〜ない
note.pt-BR: ん (de ぬ), negação que com ませ forma ません, completando めったに〜ない

objections.objection: The op fixed the inverted composition in lit_en ('is rarely carried out (rarely, is-not-carried-out)') but left lit_pt as 'Quanto a agora, raramente não é realizado.' In pt-BR that is a real double negative and reads as 'it is rarely NOT carried out' = 'it is usually carried out', i.e. the very inversion just removed from en, and the opposite of translation.pt-BR ('Hoje em dia raramente se faz isso'). After the patch the two literal fields state opposite propositions for the same sentence; pt needs the same disambiguating parenthetical en received.
objections.auditor_hint: Quanto a agora, [isso] raramente é realizado (raramente, não-é-realizado).

current.jp: 辞書はあそこの本棚にあります。
current.kana: じしょわあそこのほんだなにあります。

structure_explanation.en: The sentence follows the location pattern 'X は Y に あります' (X is in Y), used to say where an inanimate thing is located. The topic is 辞書 (dictionary), marked by は, and the place is あそこの本棚 (the bookshelf over there), marked by に. The verb ある (to exist, for lifeless objects) in the polite form あります closes the sentence. Note that あそこの本棚 uses の to link 'over there' to 'bookshelf', forming 'the bookshelf over there'.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase segue o padrão de localização 'X は Y に あります' (X está em Y), usado para dizer onde uma coisa inanimada se encontra. O tópico é 辞書 (dicionário), marcado por は, e o lugar é あそこの本棚 (a estante de ali), marcado por に. O verbo ある (existir, para objetos sem vida) na forma polida あります fecha a frase. Note que あそこの本棚 usa の para ligar 'ali' a 'estante', formando 'a estante de lá'.

translation_literal.en: The dictionary [topic] is in that bookshelf over there.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Dicionário [tópico] ali de estante em existe.

translation.pt-BR: O dicionário está naquela estante de livros ali.
translation.en: The dictionary is on that bookshelf over there.

gloss.en: over there (place distant from both speakers)
to exist, to be (for inanimate things)

note.en: connective stem of ある, to which ます is attached
note.pt-BR: raiz conetiva de ある, à qual se anexa ます

note.en: auxiliary ます, polite non-past form
note.pt-BR: auxiliar ます, forma polida não-passada

(verified in research/datasets/tatoeba/links.tar.bz2 + eng_sentences.tsv.bz2, and it is the exact string in corpus/sentences/bank.json). translation_literal.en: I wonder if it'll turn to rain, huh.

structure_explanation.en: The sentence is 雨になる ('to turn to rain', i.e. 'to rain') followed by のかしら. The の (準体助詞) nominalizes the clause and gives an explanatory/pondering tone, and かしら is the feminine final particle expressing doubt to oneself, equivalent to 'I wonder if...?'. The grammatical focus appears at the end to turn the statement into a soft, internal question.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase é 雨になる ('virar chuva', isto é, 'chover') seguida de のかしら. O の (準体助詞) nominaliza a oração e dá um tom explicativo/ponderativo, e かしら é a partícula final feminina que expressa dúvida consigo mesma, equivalente a 'será que...?'. O foco gramatical aparece no fim para transformar a afirmação numa pergunta interna e suave.

role.pt-BR: complemento de estado resultante (de なる)

gloss.en: to become (here: 'to rain', 雨になる = to start raining)
gloss.pt-BR: virar, tornar-se (aqui: 'chover', 雨になる = começar a chover)

note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário (não-passado) de なる

objections.objection: Asymmetric application of the op's own reasoning. The op removed ', né?' from lit_pt because an agreement tag misrepresents かしら (self-directed wondering, already covered by '(será que)'), but lit_en keeps the identical agreement tag: "I wonder if it'll turn to rain, huh." After the patch the en and pt literals teach かしら differently.
objections.auditor_hint: I wonder if it'll turn to rain.

structure_explanation.en: The focus そんなに ("that much") modifies the degree of the verb 急かす ("to hurry / to rush someone"). The prohibition comes from the particle な right after the verb in dictionary form (急かす + な = "don't do X"), and よ at the end reinforces the tone. Note that here な is the prohibition particle, not the negation ない.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O foco そんなに ("tanto assim") modifica o grau do verbo 急かす ("apressar / meter pressa"). A proibição vem da partícula な logo após o verbo na forma de dicionário (急かす + な = "não faça X"), e よ no fim reforça o tom. Note que aqui な é a partícula de proibição, não a negação ない.

note.en: そんな + に forming the adverb そんなに
note.pt-BR: そんな + に formando o advérbio そんなに

note.en: に that turns そんな into そんなに
note.pt-BR: に que transforma そんな em そんなに

note.en: dictionary form of 急かす (せかす), base for the prohibition with な
note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário de 急かす (せかす), base para a proibição com な

objections.objection: LAYER A VIOLATION (gen=false). translation.en is the Tatoeba human English: jpn #11041763 is linked to eng #41524 = "Don't be in such a hurry." (also linked: #12160819 "Don't be in such a rush.", #9188642 "Don't go so fast."), verified in links.tar.bz2 + eng_sentences.tsv.bz2 and identical to the string in corpus/sentences/bank.json. The patch rewrites it to 'Don't rush me so much!'. Whether or not the Tatoeba translators' reading of 急かす is the one we would pick, source en is immutable for gen=false records. As with 10987705, the diff's 'before' omits texts.translation.en, disguising an overwrite as an addition.
objections.auditor_hint: Don't be in such a hurry.

current.jp: そして、先生なんですよね？
current.kana: そして、せんせいなんですよね?

structure_explanation.en: The sentence begins with the target connective そして ('and / and furthermore'), which adds this information to something said before. The core is 先生 ('teacher') + な(=だ)+ んです, the んです structure (explanatory/confirmatory) that gives a tone of 'it's that / so'. At the end, よね combines the emphasis of よ with the agreement-seeking of ね, resulting in 'right?'.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase começa com o conector-alvo そして ('e / e além disso'), que adiciona esta informação a algo dito antes. O núcleo é 先生 ('professor') + な(=だ)+ んです, a estrutura んです (explicativa/confirmatória) que dá um tom de 'é que / então'. No fim, よね combina a ênfase de よ com a busca de concordância de ね, resultando em 'né?'.

translation_literal.en: And (you) are a teacher — that's the case, right?

note.en: な form of だ, required before ん/の in the explanatory structure んです
note.pt-BR: forma な de だ, exigida antes de ん/の na estrutura explicativa んです

note.en: polite です closing the explanatory structure んです
note.pt-BR: です polido fechando a estrutura explicativa んです

objections.objection: The rewritten translation_literal.en introduces an em dash ('And (you) are a teacher — that's the case, right?'), which is banned in learner-facing text. It is newly introduced by this patch (the 'before' string had none).
objections.auditor_hint: And (you) are a teacher, that's the case, right?
